description: Climb the West Rim Trail from the Grotto to Scout Lookout, then follow a chain-assisted ridge to the summit.
permit_note: Permit required from Scout Lookout to the summit (lottery)

description: Descend the South Rim's best-known canyon trail past the resthouses to the Colorado River and Phantom Ranch.
closure_note: Inner-canyon bridges and the North Kaibab Trail were closed for repairs on the NPS page we read; check current alerts

description: Switchbacks to Cascade Pass, then a steep climb along the Sahale Arm to the toe of Sahale Glacier.
permit_note: Backcountry camping needs a permit; permits are hard to get in busy periods
closure_note: Steep snow can need an ice axe as late as July

description: Climb from Dunraven Pass through subalpine forest to the fire lookout on the Mount Washburn summit.
closure_note: Not recommended in September and October, when grizzlies feed nearby

description: Walk through young lodgepole forest to a 200-foot waterfall.
A long, mostly exposed climb above the Many Glacier lakes to the Grinnell Glacier overlook.
closure_note: Snow fields can keep the upper trail closed until mid to late July

description: Follow the Highline Trail along the Garden Wall from Logan Pass to Granite Park Chalet.
closure_note: Snow can keep the trail closed into early summer

description: A very long day hike up the Yosemite Valley wall that ends on cables to the Half Dome summit.
permit_note: Permit required when the cables are up (lottery)
closure_note: The cables are down for the winter, usually from the day after Columbus Day until Memorial Day weekend

description: A 350-step stairway climbs a granite dome for views of the Great Western Divide.
closure_note: Do not climb when ice or snow is on the stairs

description: A steady slickrock climb past Wolfe Ranch and a petroglyph wall to the park's best-known arch.
A short walk to a cliff-edge arch that frames the canyon, popular at sunrise.
A loop from Sunrise Point down Queens Garden and up the Navajo Loop among the hoodoos.
closure_note: The Wall Street side of Navajo Loop closes when precipitation and freezing nights combine

description: A loop from Paradise through wildflower meadows to Panorama Point, with views of Mount Rainier.
closure_note: Snow covers and unmarks the trail from November to June

description: A steady stone-step climb to a summit with 360-degree views across Joshua Tree.
Follow the trail from Bear Lake past Nymph and Dream Lakes to Emerald Lake in Tyndall Gorge.
permit_note: Timed entry reservation that includes Bear Lake Road needed from late May to mid-October
closure_note: Snow and ice can cover the trail above 10,000 ft after storms

description: Hike from the Jenny Lake Trailhead past Hidden Falls to Inspiration Point.
Climb granite slopes along the north ridge to the summit of Cadillac Mountain.
A steep, rocky trail past Arch Rock and Alum Cave Bluffs to the summit of Mount LeConte.
A steep paved walk to the observation tower on Kuwohi, the highest point in the park.
closure_note: The road to the tower closes in winter

description: A flat boardwalk and paved trail through sawgrass marsh where alligators and wading birds gather.
Wade upstream through the Virgin River canyon from the Temple of Sinawava.
permit_note: No permit needed to hike up from the bottom
closure_note: Wading in the river; closed when the flow is over 150 CFS, common in spring snowmelt. Flash floods can happen at any time

description: A long climb to the summit by the Keyhole Route, with exposed scrambling above the Boulder Field.
permit_note: Timed entry reservation needed to enter the park from late May to mid-October
closure_note: Start before sunrise: the round trip averages 10 to 15 hours. The most snow-free period is generally mid-July to mid-September

description: A short paved walk to the largest tree in the world by volume.
closure_note: The trail can be icy in winter
